The gps_trace measures 22.95 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a booked optimal of 16.7 km, an excess of 6.25 km, or 37.43% of the optimal route. Both POL-RD-01 gates are cleared: the excess is greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms and greater than 20% of optimal, and both tests must pass, so a deviation exists. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing field where it disagrees with the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km (22.9 km), and on the trace figure the excess is 6.25 km, not the smaller figure the convenience copy would give.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. The trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-02830, and the trace's first fix at 17:08:27 matches trip_record.started_at, so limb (a) is satisfied. Limb (b) is satisfied by a 6.25 km excess measured from a gps_trace that is unimpaired under POL-RD-07. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, well below the 4-claim trigger, so no corroboration beyond the trace is required of this rider; and POL-GEN-01 confines the profile to the tests that name its fields, which that field does not here.

claims.text: The trace is clean, so the driver cannot retreat into the impaired-trace rules. EV-GPS-02830 carries 181 fixes at a 10 second sample interval over 100.0% coverage, with zero gaps and max_gap_sec of 0.0. It meets none of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) - no gap above 90 seconds, no straight-line jump above 500 m, no sustained interval above 30 seconds - so the deviation may be established on the trace alone and POL-RD-10(3), which escalates an impaired trace lacking independent corroboration, is not engaged.

The driver's traffic excuse carries no weight on this record. The counterparty_statement blames 'a massive jam on the expressway', but the bundle holds no traffic_advisory for this trip: EV-ADVIS-02830-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and I disclose that impairment and cite the identifier for its absence. POL-RD-13 requires the traffic assertion to be tested against the traffic_advisory and nothing else; with no advisory on file the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Because the driver names no evidence identifier for any advisory, this is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-13(1) keeps POL-RD-10(5) from firing and the case does not escalate on that ground.

No rider instruction can excuse any part of the route. The chat_log for this trip is empty - message_count 0, first_message_at and last_message_at both null, and trip_record.chat_message_count confirms it - so there is no rider message, no waypoint_hint and no requested road. POL-RD-04 is unavailable on this record and the measured excess stands undiminished; POL-RD-14's uncorroborated-instruction rule has nothing to operate on either, since no instruction was given.

The endpoints were never amended, so POL-RD-05 gives the driver no re-quote. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null, so there is no amended optimal to re-run POL-RD-01 against; the booked 16.7 km optimal route governs.

This was not a pooled trip. trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline has no application and there is no co-rider collection distance to exclude. The excess is measured against the ordinary 16.7 km optimal and stands at 6.25 km.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02 and comes to SGD 6.80. The fare_model on the fare_breakdown is METERED, so POL-RD-02 runs: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 16.7 + 0.28 x 22.5) x the surge_multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier (1.0) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP and tolls = 23.4250. Refund = charged_total 30.18 - 23.4250 = 6.755, which is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and is 22.38% of charged_total, far below the 90% share that would convert it to a full refund. The payable figure rounds UP to SGD 6.80, and the rider asks for PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 6.80.

There is no pass-through line to correct, and no second bite at the refund. erp_gantries is an empty array, tolls_erp is 0.00 and the optimal_route_erp is 0, while airport_surcharge is 0.00 and waiting_time_fee is 0.00. POL-RD-09 therefore adds nothing on top of the POL-RD-02 figure, and equally it takes nothing away: had there been off-route ERP it would already be comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund and could never be added to it a second time, and limb (4) has no unmatched gantry or wrongly applied surcharge to address.

No POL-RD-10 trigger fires and this case should be ruled, not escalated. The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07; the timestamps run forward and no two admitted artifacts disagree - pickup 17:08:27 on the trace against 17:08:27 on the trip_record, ended 17:38:27 against charged 17:38:52; the refund of 6.755 is far below both the SGD 150.00 ceiling and charged_total; every charge line has a counterpart in the trip_record; and the driver's traffic excuse is a failed assertion rather than contradictory evidence of comparable strength, per POL-RD-13(1).

The rider does not seek the POL-RD-06 uplift, and says so plainly rather than stretching the record. The deviation is not MATERIAL under POL-RD-01 - 37.43% and 6.25 km sit below the 50% and 8.0 km material thresholds - and on the fields POL-RD-06 names, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against completed_trips_90d of 395, so neither the count of 3 or more nor the 0.05 ratio test is met and no pattern is established. The rider's remedy is accordingly the POL-RD-02 partial refund computed above, not a full refund of charged_total.
